title: A retraction base change preserves absence of quasi-finite closed-fibre points
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, let $R'$ be a commutative $R$-algebra, and let $\tau:R'\to R$ be an $R$-algebra homomorphism. Let $P\subset R'$ be a prime ideal satisfying $P=\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$. Let $C$ be a finite-type $R'$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $B$ be a finite-type $R$-algebra. Give $R$ its $R'$-algebra structure via $\tau$, and suppose there is an $R$-algebra isomorphism $R\otimes_{R'}C\cong B$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. If $R'\to C$ is not quasi-finite at any prime over $P$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], then $R\to B$ is not quasi-finite at any prime over $\mathfrak m$. Neither $C$ nor $B$ is assumed nonzero, and the ring universes are independent.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04GG, proof of (8) => (11), final sentence; the omitted fibre verification is expanded using the tensor quotient spectrum embedding. Source read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04GG.

proof.text: Use the splitting tau(algebraMap(r)) = r to prove tau surjective. Mathlib Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_surjective makes C -> R tensor_{R'} C surjective. Compose with the given equivalence to obtain f : C -> B. PrimeSpectrum.isEmbedding_comap_of_surjective gives an embedding Spec B -> Spec C. The coefficient composite is f(algebraMap_{R',C}(a)) = algebraMap_{R,B}(tau(a)).

For a prime q of C over P, extend C -> kappa(q) [def-weil-residue-field] to the tensor algebra. The R-coefficient map sends r to the residue of its image under R -> R' -> C. It is R'-linear because algebraMap(tau(a)) - a lies in ker(tau), hence in P and q. TensorProduct.lift supplies the extension. Compose with the inverse product-factor equivalence to get g : B -> kappa(q) with g o f equal to the residue map. Therefore ker(f) is contained in q. By range_comap_of_surjective, every such q belongs to the image of Spec B -> Spec C.

The preimage under Spec(f) of the fibre over P equals the fibre of Spec B over m: contraction of an ideal along the surjection tau is injective, and P = tau^{-1}(m). Restrict the spectrum embedding using Topology.IsEmbedding.homeomorphOfSubsetRange. This constructs a homeomorphism between the two fibres.

Unfold [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] and use PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber to identify quasi-finiteness with openness of a singleton in the fibre subspace. If q of B over m were quasi-finite, its open singleton would map through the restricted homeomorphism to an open singleton in the fibre of C over P. This contradicts the hypothesis on C. Empty fibre spectra and zero factors require no special case.

lean.statement:
theorem no_quasiFiniteAtPrime_of_retraction_baseChange
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    {R' : Type w} [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    (τ : R' →ₐ[R] R) (P : Ideal R') [P.IsPrime]
    (hP : P = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).comap τ.toRingHom)
    (C : Type x) [CommRing C] [Algebra R' C] [Algebra.FiniteType R' C]
    (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra.FiniteType R B] :
    letI : Algebra R' R := τ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    ∀ (_e : (R ⊗[R'] C) ≃ₐ[R] B),
      (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum C, q.asIdeal.LiesOver P → ¬ IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime R' C q) →
      ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
        q.comap (algebraMap R B) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R →
          ¬ IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime R B q
